Its tracker, inherited from SAM 2, stores information from past frames in a memory bank, managed by a simple First-In-First-Out rule, allowing temporal consistency in complex videos. Several recent methods improve SAM 2 with hand-crafted memory update rules, each targeting a specific failure mode, such as distractors, occlusions, or object motion. However, their gains transfer only partially to the stronger SAM 3 backbone. We instead present a more general, data-driven approach that frames memory control as a sequential decision-making task. SAM3RL is an extension of the SAM 3 tracker with a lightweight memory controller, trained by reinforcement learning, that decides which frames enter the memory bank in order to maximize tracking performance. SAM3RL sets a new state of the art on 10 of 12 tracking and video object segmentation benchmarks, outperforming all hand-crafted rules without any runtime overhead. The same approach applied to SAM 2 gives SAM2RL, which outperforms hand-crafted rules on 9 of the 12 benchmarks, showing the generality of our method across model generations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: TimeWarp: Evaluating Web Agents by Revisiting the Past
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: As web agents close the gap with humans on benchmarks, one question arises: Do today's agents perform just as well on tomorrow's web? We introduce TimeWarp, a benchmark that emulates the evolving web. TimeWarp consists of three web environments, each with six UI versions spanning UI design, frontend code, and workflows from different eras of the internet. We pair TimeWarp with a set of complex, realistic tasks covering different forms of web navigation. Our experiments reveal that vision-based agents are vulnerable to changes, while text-based agents become brittle once fine-tuned on a single version. To address this, we propose TimeTraj, a new annotation method that uses plan distillation to collect trajectories across multiple versions. By training agents on teacher rollouts using our BC-variant, we achieve substantial performance gains: 20.4% to 37.7% for Qwen-3 4B and 0% to 27.0% for Llama-3.1 8B models. Our work helps study generalization across web designs and opens a new paradigm for collecting plans rather than trajectories to improve the robustness of web agents.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Quantifying Annotation Agreement in Object Detection with Optimal Transport
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Reliable validation of machine learning models is a crucial step in designing robust and trustworthy systems. Yet validation relies on annotated test sets treated as ground truth, even though annotations can be noisy or ambiguous. In object detection, sources may disagree on object presence, box location, or class label. Standard agreement metrics usually binarize box overlap before computing a summary score, obscuring the degree and structure of disagreement between annotation sets. Here, we study an Optimal Transport (OT)-based metric for measuring agreement between object detection annotations. Instead of binarizing bounding box overlap, this metric assigns graded costs to matched and unmatched labeled boxes. Through theoretical analysis and experiments on real and synthetically perturbed annotations, we show that OT captures graded changes in agreement and distinguishes annotation pairs that thresholded metrics score identically. Our results suggest that OT provides a richer measure of annotation agreement in object detection, especially for domains with many small or ambiguous objects. Such agreement estimates can support more reliable validation when labels are noisy or conflicting.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CARD: Closing the Teacher-Student Loop for Adversarial Robustness Distillation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Adversarial robustness distillation typically treats a robust teacher as a fixed knowledge source and transfers robustness to a compact student in a one-way manner. This paradigm terminates teacher-student interaction once the student is distilled, thereby discarding potentially useful feedback from the distilled student. However, exploiting such feedback is nontrivial because indiscriminate weak-to-strong transfer may propagate student errors to the teacher. To address this issue, we propose Cyclic Adversarial Robustness Distillation (CARD), a closed-loop framework that turns the distilled student into a feedback source for refining the robust teacher and subsequently transfers the teacher gains back to the same student. CARD first performs strong-to-weak adversarial distillation and then uses reliability-enhanced student feedback to refine the robust teacher. The refinement combines inverse adversarial student feedback with teacher-student discrepancy maximization, after which the refined teacher is used to continue training the same student under the unchanged base distillation objective. We further establish a sample-level sufficient condition for reliable weak-to-strong feedback transfer and derive a distribution-level upper bound on the refined teacher's risk. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet-10 across multiple teacher-student architectures and base distillation methods show that CARD improves adversarial robustness in most evaluated settings while generally preserving clean accuracy. These results show that the distilled student can provide useful feedback to the teacher, enabling robustness transfer to proceed beyond the conventional one-way teacher-to-student paradigm.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Multimodal Medical Image Parsing with Task-Specific Low-Rank Adapters
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Adapting a single vision-language model to medical image parsing requires training choices that reflect the demands of each task. We study task-specific adaptation with Qwen3.5-9B for FLARE 2026 Task 3, covering six task families and seven imaging modalities. Our system couples a shared, frozen 4-bit backbone with LoRA adapters selected from the input question. We customize adapter ranks and prompts, rebalance rare classification targets, and supplement regression training with dermatology classification examples. On the fixed internal holdout, the task-specific adapters achieve a dataset-macro balanced accuracy of 0.7791 for classification, a dataset-macro micro-F1 of 0.6286 for multi-label classification, a counting mean absolute error (MAE) of 11.73, a dataset-macro detection F1 of 0.8914, a dataset-macro regression MAE of 9.78, and a report-generation CRIMSON score of 0.8204. On the organizer's 1,703-example hidden-validation set, the submitted system achieves 0.8496 classification balanced accuracy, 0.5338 sample-averaged multi-label F1, and 14.5950 regression MAE. The final 30.1 GB container averages 3.1 seconds per case, including model loading, and produces identical outputs across repeated verification runs. The benefits vary across tasks, supporting the use of task-specific adapter configurations and image budgets within a shared medical vision-language model. Code is available at https://github.com/TahaSabir0/FLARE26-Hexapus.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 17 pages, 4 figures. FLARE 2026 Task 3 methodology paper (2D track)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: On the Limits of Representation-Based Test-Time Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-language models suffer significant accuracy drops under common corruptions. While test-time adaptation (TTA) successfully mitigates these shifts in CLIP-like contrastive models, its application to generative multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains underexplored and uniquely challenging due to their sequential token generation. In this work, we demonstrate that representation-based TTA fails to recover performance in MLLMs. Our experiments reveal that even when violating standard TTA assumptions by leveraging target data offline, sample-blind feature alignment recovers only marginal accuracy. We attribute this failure to the nature of corruption shifts: unlike CLIP-like architectures, which benefit from a shared domain-shift direction within a single pooled classification embedding, MLLM visual token sequence shifts are nearly orthogonal and span the full embedding space.These findings bound what any sample-blind, position-shared correction at a single encoder site can achieve, establishing that representation-space interventions alone might be insufficient to ensure corruption robustness in MLLMs.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted at the Grounded and Faithful Vision-Language Models for Real-World Deployment (VLM4RWD) workshop at NeurIPS 2026

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: BluePixel: Toward Native 4K Agentic Image Editing
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Instruction-driven image editing has reached native 4K, yet how such editors are trained remains undisclosed, and pretraining one from scratch is beyond most teams. The task itself compounds the difficulty: a single end-to-end editor cannot make precise parametric adjustments, match specialized experts, or interpret the vague instructions users actually write. We argue that 4K editing is a system problem rather than a single-model problem, and present BluePixel, which couples a native-4K editing model with an agent harness; the complete training recipe is disclosed in this paper. The model makes 4K training practical: it turns a 1K-pretrained editor into a native-4K one through progressive VAE adaptation that keeps 4K training as affordable as 1K, absorbs a long tail of vertical editing skills through continual learning, and refines the aesthetic-fidelity trade-off with reinforcement learning. Distillation via source-anchored target projection (SATP) then compresses 50 denoising steps to 4, completing a 4K edit in 8.7 s on a single Kunlunxin P800 XPU while preserving task success rate and background consistency. The harness, BluePixel Agent, makes editing controllable: it decomposes user instructions into specialist and general operations, verifies every result with the same reward model that guided training, and retries within bounded attempts. On VINS-4KEval++ (3,305 native-4K cases), BluePixel ranks second among seven models, behind only GPT Image 2 in non-edited-region consistency.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CoDy: Codec Dynamics as Complementary Priors for Unsupervised Temporal Action Localization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Unsupervised temporal action localization (UTAL) aims to identify action categories and localize their temporal boundaries without annotation supervision. Existing methods typically derive supervision for both tasks solely from RGB and optical-flow representations, often resulting in noisy category assignments and inaccurate temporal boundaries. In this work, we reveal an overlooked property of video codecs: group-of-pictures quantization patterns preserve category-discriminative dynamics, while motion-vector and residual variations exhibit pronounced responses around action transitions. Based on this insight, we propose CoDy, a codec dynamics-guided framework that exploits the codec as complementary information to the visual view for UTAL. CoDy integrates a codec-enhanced view with RGB and flow through confidence-aware consensus clustering, producing reliable soft pseudo-labels. It further converts codec dynamics into a class-agnostic boundary prior, which supervises visual boundary learning and guides proposal initialization and iterative refinement. The codec branches are only used during the training stage and introduce no extra codec-side computation at inference. Extensive experiments on THUMOS14 and ActivityNet v1.3 demonstrate that CoDy consistently outperforms existing UTAL methods and achieves state-of-the-art localization performance. These results establish codec signals as effective annotation-free priors for jointly inferring which actions occur and when they occur.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CorrelationFlow: A Training-Free Geometric Approach for LiDAR Scene Flow Estimation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: LiDAR scene flow is the task of estimating point-wise motion from sequential point clouds. It is essential for autonomous driving, as it provides critical information about moving objects and their trajectories. In recent years, unsupervised methods have gained significant traction by eliminating the need for expensive point-wise annotations. However, despite incremental performance improvements, these methods uniformly rely on a single paradigm: training feed-forward networks through optimizing a loss function based on the Chamfer distance, a framework that inherently limits their progression. This paper presents CorrelationFlow, a new paradigm that reformulates LiDAR scene flow as a correlation maximization problem between Bird's-Eye View (BEV) images. Instead of using learnable parameters, our approach employs a chain of image processing operations to solve this problem. The learning-free nature of CorrelationFlow enables strong generalization across diverse domains. This capability is demonstrated by the second-place ranking in the unsupervised track of the Argoverse 2 Scene Flow Challenge at CVPR 2026, which featured a test set spanning five datasets that cover varied vehicle platforms and environments. Our results show that this classical, model-based approach can match or even surpass the performance of learning-based methods, thereby opening a new direction for unsupervised LiDAR scene flow research. The source code will be released.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Colon3R: Cross-Domain 3D Reconstruction from Monocular Colonoscopic Video
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Monocular colonoscopic 3D reconstruction is important for surgical robotic colonoscopy, but remains challenging due to weak texture, specular reflections, limited view overlap, and non-rigid tissue motion. Conventional multi-view 3D reconstruction methods rely on stable correspondences and approximate rigidity, which are often violated in colonoscopy. Existing endoscopic methods often rely on domain-specific supervision, whereas there are not enough in-vivo labeled data available to adapt geometry foundation models to clinical colonoscopy. We present Colon3R, a cross-domain semi-supervised framework built on pretrained VGGT that transfers coupled camera, depth, and pointmap geometry from labeled phantom and simulated data to unlabeled in-vivo colonoscopy without requiring target-domain geometric annotations. Unlike source-only fine-tuning, which learns only from phantom and simulated data, Colon3R directly exploits unlabeled in-vivo video through teacher-derived cross-view supervision. Our proposed hierarchical quasi-rigid reliability selects reliable supervision at the sequence, directed-pair, and pixel levels, while source-preserving adaptation retains the learned coupled geometry during target-domain adaptation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior overall performance over state-of-the-art approaches in depth, pointmap, and camera pose estimation. Qualitative comparisons on real in-vivo colonoscopy further show substantially more complete and geometrically consistent reconstructions than competing methods under clinical domain shift. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/vglx/Colon3R.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Synergistic Vision-Language Reinforcement Enables Scalable On-Demand Analysis across Diverse Clinical Tasks
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Accurate segmentation of tumors and organs-at-risk is essential for oncology but remains time-consuming and expertise-intensive. Existing AI systems often require manual spatial prompts or task-specific retraining, while generic class labels provide limited guidance for heterogeneous disease targets. Here we present SyRe, a text-prompted segmentation foundation model based on Synergistic vision-language Reinforcement, which strengthens bidirectional interaction between visual and linguistic representations. We introduce Color Region Description (CRD) to generate region-level semantic supervision and construct SyReData, comprising 20 million image-mask-description triplets across 9 modalities and 229 segmentation tasks. Training with diversified prompt formats enables single-target, multi-target and open-ended segmentation, together with invalid-prompt rejection. SyRe achieves accurate segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios, with strong gains on disease-related targets. Evaluation on 28 unseen external datasets, including 17 cancer types, 3 non-cancer diseases and multinational in-house cohorts, demonstrates generalization under distribution shift. Beyond spatial overlap, SyRe-generated masks preserve quantitative pathology information. Across five retrospective tumor imaging cohorts spanning CT and MRI, radiomics derived from these masks stratify survival and improve prognostic modeling over clinical baselines. Clinician-in-the-loop refinement further supports case-level correction. These results establish SyRe as a generalizable framework for scalable quantitative oncology analysis and clinician-guided segmentation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: OmniPoser: Flexible Human Motion Recovery in the Wild with Masked Flow Matching
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recovering 3D human motion from sparse wearable sensors is challenging due to the inherent noise, occlusion, and instability of real-world tracking signals. Existing approaches are restricted to fixed sensor configurations and, when built on diffusion models, are computationally prohibitive for real-time deployment. We propose OmniPoser, a universal framework that recovers full-body SMPL motion from a flexible combination of heterogeneous inputs, such as 3D keypoints, sparse IMU rotations, head-mounted 6-DoF poses, or any subset thereof, within a single model. OmniPoser introduces a cross-modal masking mechanism paired with a Masked Conditioning Encoder, enabling one architecture to incorporate diverse sensor configurations through a masked design. A decoupled dual-stream generative backbone generates complete motion via Conditional Flow Matching, requiring only a single ODE integration step at inference. Across three settings and seven benchmarks, including in-the-wild Nymeria and Ego-Exo4D datasets, OmniPoser performs on par with state-of-the-art methods while running at over 700 FPS. The project page is available at https://jamesbridgewater51.github.io/omniposer-eccv/.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted as a poster at the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: GAE: Learning a Geometry-Native Latent Space for 3D-Consistent World Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We present a compact geometry-native latent space as a shared foundation for perception and generation. Visual generators can produce photorealistic frames without preserving a consistent 3D scene. We argue that this is not only a modeling problem but also a representation problem: generators typically evolve appearance-centric latents, while perception models recover geometry in a semantically rich space that encodes cross-view structure. Rather than adding geometry as another output, we reparameterize a geometry foundation model's features into a compact latent space for generation. We realize this shift with the geometry-native autoencoder (GAE), whose latent is jointly decodable to appearance, depth, cameras, and point maps. With this state, a standard conditional flow supports diverse generation tasks. In controlled comparisons that hold the generator and training protocol fixed, replacing the latent with GAE improves both visual quality and independently measured 3D coherence: FVD falls by $12.7\%$ and $23.1\%$ on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, and camera-trajectory error is halved on RealEstate10K. Together, these results show that the latent space is central to geometry-consistent generation and can serve as a shared interface between perception and generation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DeltaStreamer: Towards Human-Like Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
We propose DeltaStreamer, a novel agentic framework for streaming video understanding inspired by how humans observe, remember, and investigate. Streaming video understanding requires a system to retain evidence before knowing which details future queries will need. Existing approaches often obscure event transitions and omit relevant details when compressing video history, and cannot recover missing visual evidence. DeltaStreamer addresses these limitations by combining change-aware memory with query-driven planning and targeted evidence gathering with replay. Before a query arrives, it continuously observes the stream and explicitly records visual changes in structured memory, preserving how events unfold rather than only what is present. When a query arrives, a query-driven planner identifies the required evidence and guides memory retrieval and targeted replay. By revisiting historical frames, the agent can recover visual details omitted during observation and ground its answer in evidence beyond the retained descriptions. This connects continuous observation with active investigation tailored to each question. Experiments on OVO-Bench and StreamingBench demonstrate improvements over representative streaming video understanding methods, with overall scores of 66.07% and 59.53%, respectively.
  Project page: https://bbbbchan.github.io/DeltaStreamer/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: VisibilitySplat: Ray-Traced Occlusion for Relighting with 3D Gaussian Splatting
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We address inverse rendering with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) by introducing explicit visibility modeling for relighting as well as material and light decomposition. Our approach augments the standard rasterized 3DGS pipeline with a sparse visibility oracle that estimates transmittance-weighted occlusion for Gaussian primitives from sampled lighting directions. This oracle is implemented using a point-based ray tracer accelerated by a bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) and queried sparsely within the inverse-rendering objectives, while the original 3DGS loop is retained for training efficiency, interactive visualization, and tooling compatibility. Shading follows a physically based rendering (PBR) formulation with a principled microfacet bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) and low-resolution high-dynamic-range (HDR) environment maps. We evaluate our method on the TensoIR synthetic dataset against baselines based on neural radiance fields (NeRFs), tensor representations, and 3DGS. The results show competitive performance and improvements over several earlier baselines for novel-view synthesis (NVS), albedo reconstruction, and relighting. Ablations indicate that explicit visibility modeling is an important contributor to relighting and material-illumination disentanglement, while pure PBR supervision can favor appearance fitting in NVS. Overall, the findings suggest that sparse, point-based visibility queries effectively complement rasterized splatting for inverse rendering while preserving the practical advantages of the 3DGS ecosystem.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Published at WSCG 2026

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DarKnight: Retrieval-Guided Agentic Framework for Breaking Dark Web CAPTCHA Gates
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) investigators who monitor dark web marketplaces for leaked credentials and breach listings must pass the diverse CAPTCHAs that operators deploy to block automated collection. Existing solvers either need unscalable per-site fine-tuning or rely on commercial Vision-Language Model (VLM) APIs, which surrender operational sovereignty: provider policies, Tor-exit blocking, government regulation, or model updates outside the investigator's control can halt or alter the solver overnight, and per-call costs recur with every session and retry. We present DarKnight, a self-improving agentic framework designed to run on a single workstation GPU inside an investigator's Tor crawler and solve CAPTCHAs with small, locally hosted open-weight VLMs that no provider decision can withdraw, without per-market training or third-party services. For each CAPTCHA, DarKnight retrieves successful and failed past attempts on similar images (dual-signal RAG), composes an image-specific preprocessing pipeline, and learns from the site's pass/fail verdict. In a case study on four real-world dark web marketplaces, agentic tool selection outperformed parameter scaling. A deployable open-weight VLM with DarKnight reached 83.2\% on the most heavily defended market, 37.2 percentage points above its base model, outperforming even the frontier Claude Opus~5 (44%). DarKnight recovered 48.2% of baseline failures at a 7.6% degeneration cost, indicating that selective tool use can avoid much of the degradation caused by uniform preprocessing.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Schrödinger's Navigator: Imagining an Ensemble of Futures for Zero-Shot Object Navigation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Zero-shot object navigation (ZSON) requires robots to find target objects in unseen environments without task-specific fine-tuning or pre-built maps, a key capability for general-purpose service robots. Yet methods that perform well in simulation often degrade in cluttered real-world scenes with severe occlusion and latent hazards, where large unseen regions make single-scene inference brittle and unsafe. We propose Schrödinger's Navigator, a belief-aware framework that reasons at inference time over multiple trajectory-conditioned imagined 3D futures. Given candidate paths, a trajectory-conditioned 3D world model predicts hypothetical observations and maintains a superposition of plausible scene realizations rather than committing to one map. An adaptive occluder-aware sampler directs imagination to uncertainty-critical regions, while a Future-Aware Value Map (FAVM) aggregates imagined futures for robust, proactive action selection. Experiments in simulation and on a physical Go2 quadruped show that Schrödinger's Navigator outperforms strong ZSON baselines, improving hidden-target discovery and risk-aware waypoint selection in occlusion-heavy navigation scenarios. These results highlight imagined 3D futures as a scalable and generalizable strategy for zero-shot navigation in uncertain real-world environments.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: What Matters for World Modeling in Vision-Language-Action Models?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Integrating world models into Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) has emerged as a promising direction, enabling policies to anticipate future dynamics beyond reactive observation-to-action mapping. However, existing approaches vary simultaneously in their world representations, integration paradigms, and policy backbones, making it difficult to determine what truly matters for effective world model integration. To disentangle these factors, we categorize existing efforts into four representative paradigms, namely Implicit Future Alignment, Explicit Future Query, MoT Future Expert, and External World Predictor. We instantiate each within a unified framework and systematically evaluate these paradigms with diverse world representations and policy backbones across in-domain, out-of-domain, long-horizon, dynamic, few-shot, and real-world settings. Our study yields four main findings: 1) world representation effectiveness is paradigm-dependent, whereas 2D semantic representations offer robust, cross-paradigm gains; 2) no single paradigm is universally optimal, yet the decoupled MoT Future Expert offers competitive overall performance, particularly in OOD robustness; 3) world modeling consistently benefits policies built on standard VLMs, while decoupled designs exhibit greater compatibility with pretrained VLAs; and 4) world modeling improves performance over action-only baselines across multiple settings, with notable gains on long-horizon and dynamic tasks. Project page and video demonstrations are available at https://dylanmqs.github.io/WM-in-VLAs/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PhyMetric: Diagnosing Physical Plausibility in Text-to-Video Generation via Scene-Level QA
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Text-to-video (T2V) generation models can produce visually realistic videos that nevertheless violate the physical consequences implied by the prompt and scene. Existing benchmarks largely rely on holistic plausibility scores or broad quality dimensions, leaving it unclear which physical behavior is being tested and why a model fails. We introduce PhyMetric, a scene-level diagnostic benchmark that recasts physical plausibility evaluation as verifiable, scene-grounded question answering. PhyMetric contains 1{,}115 scenes spanning 50 physical categories across six domains, paired with 8{,}920 answer-balanced binary questions over 12 evaluation dimensions. Each scene is associated with eight targeted yes/no questions and a structured physical prior specifying the governing law, expected temporal sequence, observable signatures, and common failure modes. At evaluation time, a vision-language model (VLM) judge answers each question from question-aware sampled frames conditioned on the prior, and correctness is hierarchically aggregated into scene, dimension, physical category, and model scores. Experiments on four open-source T2V models and three VLM judges show that scene-specific binary QA is a critical component of the protocol: when each targeted question is replaced by a single generic plausibility query, evaluator accuracy drops to the chance level. Structured physical priors offer a complementary signal that improves human alignment of the resulting scores, with effects that vary across VLM judges of different capacity. These findings establish PhyMetric as a benchmark that turns physical plausibility evaluation from opaque holistic scoring into interpretable, scene-level inspection. Our project page is available at: https://mengsiwei.github.io/PhyMetric/.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: This work is accepted by NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Improving Category-Aware Active Domain Adaptation via Uncertainty-Guided Region Coverage
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Active domain adaptation researches focus on alleviating the annotation cost, which comprises source data and target data labelling, as well as enhancing the performance of unsupervised domain adaptation. However, optimizing the adaptation model based on the average accuracy can lead to the drop in performance of some difficult categories. To overcome this issue, a point-wise selection strategy built upon the influence function can be used to improve domain adaptation performance. In our work, we first address the sensitive and redundant aspects of point-wise selection, which can lead to overfitting of the acquisition function. We thus introduce a region-based approach that ensures the improvement of the adaptation model by maximizing a positive manifold coverage. An uncertainty score is further introduced to the selection mechanism to learn a better decision boundary for the target domain. In comprehensive experiments, our proposed method surpasses the first category-aware active domain adaptation baseline as well as existing active domain adaptation methods across multiple domain adaptation benchmarks. Our implementation is available at: https://github.com/nhtm2702/WHO IS NEXT.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted at Machine Learning Journal through ACML Journal Track 2026

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Task-Driven Subspace Decomposition for Knowledge Sharing and Isolation in LoRA-based Continual Learning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Continual Learning (CL) requires models to sequentially adapt to new tasks without forgetting old knowledge. Recently, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a representative Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) method, has gained increasing attention in CL. Several LoRA-based CL methods reduce interference across tasks by separating their update spaces, typically building the new space from the estimated null space of past tasks. However, they (i) overlook task-shared directions, which suppresses knowledge transfer, and (ii) fail to capture truly effective task-specific directions since these ``null bases" of old tasks can remain nearly inactive for new task under correlated tasks. To address this, we study LoRA learning capability from a projection energy perspective, and propose Low-rank Decomposition and Adaptation (LoDA). It performs a task-driven decomposition to build general and truly task-specific LoRA subspaces by solving two energy-based objectives, decoupling directions for knowledge sharing and isolation. LoDA fixes LoRA down-projections on two subspaces and learns robust up-projections via a Gradient-Aligned Optimization (GAO) approach. After each task, before integrating the LoRA updates into the backbone, LoDA derives a closed-form recalibration for the general update, approximating a feature-level joint optimum along this task-shared direction. Experiments indicate that LoDA outperforms existing CL methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/HHHLF/LoDA_ICML2026.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: StateCraft: Augmenting Video World Models with Abstract-State Reasoning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Video world models aim to simulate complex environments with realistic appearance and dynamics. Maintaining consistency over long interactions requires tracking past actions and understanding how those actions affect the environment. Video world models can only generate partial observations of the entire world at a time. Remembering past observations alone may not be sufficient in every scenario, as they may no longer reflect the world after a sequence of actions. We introduce a paradigm that decouples a persistent, updatable abstract state from the visual state. The abstract state keeps track of the entities' changes as the world evolves, and is used to condition the visual state, which represents the current view. We propose StateCraft, a novel architecture that pairs a language model with a video diffusion model to evolve the dynamic world. We evaluate our approach on generative interfaces, which pose a substantial challenge because a single action may change parts of the state that are not currently visible. To support training and evaluation, we develop a data collection pipeline that produces informative, densely annotated trajectories at scale without human or agent supervision, together with a benchmark measuring generation quality, memory, and controllability. On this benchmark, our approach improves surpasses the state-of-the-art baselines. We demonstrate that StateCraft maintains high self-consistency and strong generation quality over long trajectories. Because the abstract state is explicit, it can be edited directly, and generation follows edits to states never observed in the data. Finally, a proof-of-concept 3D experiment, in which actions change the illumination of an unobserved room, shows that the paradigm can also be applied to spatial environments. Project page: https://insait-institute.github.io/StateCraft/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: 4DVLT: Dynamic Scene Understanding with Worldline-Centered Vision-Language Tracking
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Language-guided dynamic scene understanding requires identifying one physical entity across time, metric 3D space, and multiple viewpoints, a setting not captured by current multimodal reasoning or tracking paradigms. We introduce 4DVLT, an offline calibrated multi-view task that unifies grounding with metric 3D and synchronized 2D tracking through a worldline binding identity, motion, visibility, and observations. We construct Instruct-4D, with 129.4K QA pairs, 64.7K targets, 851 scenes, and 9 reasoning types, and propose 4DTrack for query-conditioned inference over a 4D state graph. 4DTrack reaches 55.18 WQS, exceeding the strongest adapted VLT baseline by 33.01 points while improving grounding and trajectory quality. The project page is available at https://github.com/mikubaka88/4DVLT.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LiFi: LiDAR Generation from Multi-View Images via Geometric and Semantic Collaborative Guidance
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Generating LiDAR point clouds from multi-view camera images is a valuable task with applications in controllable data synthesis, cross-modal simulation and various perception tasks. However, most existing methods are not specifically designed for this task, and the quality of their generated LiDAR remains limited. Moreover, these methods typically focus only on semantic cues in images or generate LiDAR from a monocular camera image. In this work, we introduce LiFi (LiDAR From images), a dedicated framework for generating visually and geometrically aligned LiDAR scenes from multi-view camera images. LiFi guides the latent diffusion process through two complementary branches: geometry and semantics. The geometry branch constructs scene features from images through a reverse sampling algorithm and an uncertainty-aware geometric encoder combined with DepthAnything3, whereas the semantic branch provides high-level semantic representations via a cross-view interaction module. We further introduce a dual-branch balanced classifier-free guidance (CFG) strategy, which enhances the model's conditional generation capability while preserving the independent learning and collaborative controllability of the two branches. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LiFi outperforms state-of-the-art methods in generating high-fidelity LiDAR scenes. The code will be publicly available at: https://github.com/szzhou88/LiFi.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: VGGT-Diff: Visual Geometry Meets Diffusion for Sparse-View Novel View Synthesis
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We present VGGT-Diff, a geometry-routed multi-view diffusion model for sparse-view novel view synthesis. Existing novel view synthesis (NVS) methods face a fundamental trade-off: reconstruction-based approaches preserve observed geometry but struggle to synthesize unseen regions, while diffusion-based methods provide strong generative priors yet rely on implicit source-to-query correspondence. VGGT-Diff bridges these regimes by routing visual geometry latents from VGGT-Ω into a pretrained video diffusion model. Each visual token is associated with a 3D point and confidence, then transformed into query-aligned latent conditions through a confidence-aware Visual Geometry Router (VGR) that preserves front and back surface evidence. These conditions guide joint target-view denoising, while Point-Track Residual Consistency (PTRC) regularizes predicted-clean residuals along reliable 3D tracks, improving multi-view stability. We further introduce robust geometry conditioning, combining training-time regularization with inference-time guidance for improved robustness. Experiments show competitive or state-of-the-art performance across interpolation and extrapolation under different viewpoint difficulties. Our code is available at https://github.com/chenkangjie1123/VGGT-Diff.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: FPV-CRASH: A Dataset for Offline Crash Moment Localization in Drone First-Person-View Videos
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Crash Moment Localization aims to localize the major physical impact that interrupts controlled flight in an onboard first-person-view (FPV) video recorded by a drone, thereby providing a temporal reference for retrospective crash analysis in aerial robotics. However, existing crash-video datasets predominantly target surveillance or dash-camera footage, and their annotation schemes and task formulations are not designed for temporal localization of the major physical impact in UAV onboard FPV videos. To address this gap, we present FPV-CRASH, a dataset and fixed-protocol reference evaluation for offline Crash Moment Localization in drone FPV videos. FPV-CRASH contains 1,052 drone FPV clips (526 Crash and 526 Normal); each Crash clip has a single-frame reference annotation for the Crash Moment, and every clip is paired with four English captions automatically generated from sampled frames and the known Crash/Normal label. Normal clips carry no timestamp target and provide training-time background supervision. The captions support an auxiliary Text-to-Video Retrieval task, whereas localization inference remains video-only. We further provide a heatmap-based reference model that estimates a continuous Crash Moment timestamp from sparsely sampled frames. Under the fixed, non-source-disjoint clip-level protocol, the reference model reduces MAE from 1.12 s for the strongest fixed timing-prior baseline to 0.56 s (a 50% relative reduction) and achieves a median absolute error (MedAE) of 0.33 s; the fraction of clips localized within 0.5 s rises from 37.14% to 65.71%. The release includes annotations, available source video identifiers and URLs, clipping metadata, fixed split lists, and preprocessing code so that the reportable portion can be reconstructed without redistributing source footage. At submission time, all source-compilation URLs remained accessible.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Computational compressive imaging reconstruction with a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Computational compressive imaging, such as single-pixel imaging and lensless imaging, is a promising imaging technique, enabling the reconstruction of objects from under-sampled measurements through compressed sensing algorithms or deep learning methods. However, the demand for electronic computational resources grows rapidly when recovering high-resolution and multi-dimensional images and training neural networks with numerous parameters, which has become a bottleneck for the widespread adoption of this technique. Here, we propose a physics-driven reconstruction framework that formulates imaging inverse problems as Ising models and directly recovers target objects through the self-evolution of non-von Neumann Ising machines toward the ground state of the Hamiltonian. We employ a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver to demonstrate this proof-of-concept by reconstructing objects in both single-pixel imaging and a lensless diffuser camera at sampling rates ranging from 1% to 25%. By further incorporating a foreground-sparsity constraint and a smoothness constraint, the reconstruction quality of our method is comparable to or even better than that of mainstream algorithms. This approach has the potential to substantially reduce the electronic computational burden of inverse reconstruction, paving the way for real-time, low-power computational imaging.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Q-MAGIC: Quad-only Mesh Autoregressive Generation via Singularity-Aware Circular Relative Offset Tokenization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Autoregressive models have proven effective for triangular mesh generation by transforming it into predicting the next face, converting the non-differentiable connectivity prediction into a sequence of token predictions. However, generating quad-only meshes remains challenging because quad faces impose stricter topological constraints than triangles. The model must not only serialize quad faces into a valid token sequence, but also support unambiguous connectivity reconstruction during de-serialization. To address this, we propose Q-MAGIC, a novel autoregressive model for quad mesh generation. We first introduce a tailored serialization scheme for quad meshes, which requires at least two new vertices for the next face and is less flexible than triangles due to strict wiring constraints. To meet these requirements and reduce serialization length, we propose a singularity-aware serialization that prioritizes wiring from singular points, leading to more coherent traversals. Additionally, we propose a circular relative offset tokenization that encodes geometry mainly via local relative offsets. Built upon this representation, an autoregressive Transformer learns the underlying distribution of quad meshes via next-token prediction, enabling effective quad mesh generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Q-MAGIC produces more compact sequences while consistently improving geometric fidelity and mesh quality compared to state-of-the-art methods.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Physics-Shaped, Not Physical: Auditing Physics-Guided Underwater Image Restoration
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Physics-guided networks for underwater image restoration predict transmission and backscatter and invert the image-formation model, yet rarely test whether this physics does any work. We audit one representative design, PhysGuide-Net, with four controlled experiments: five-seed ablations on UIEB with zero-shot evaluation on the complete LSUI (4279 pairs) and AUIED3K (3000 pairs) sets; a data-efficiency study with a capacity-matched control that removes the formation model; and a validation of the predicted maps against measured range on Sea-thru. With all 800 training images the physics module gives no zero-shot gain (mean PSNR differences of at most 0.16 dB; all 95% intervals include zero) at 3.4x the FLOPs. With 80 images it helps more (+0.65 dB on UIEB, +1.48 dB on AUIED3K; seed-to-seed s.d. on AUIED3K from 1.3 to 0.5 dB), although not individually significant after correction, and the control does not reproduce this (0.8-1.0 dB lower). Yet the predicted transmission does not behave like a physical quantity: its correlation with range is no stronger than for the range map of a different image (pooled difference +0.02, versus -0.06 for the dark-channel prior), and a Beer-Lambert fit explains 0.4% of its variance. The effect of the module also changes sign with degradation severity between datasets. The benefit thus comes from a physics-shaped inductive bias, not from physics. We further show that single-run ablations can reverse sign and document implementation defects that invalidate loss ablations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Video deep research aims to answer questions by jointly understanding video content and retrieving external knowledge from the open Web. However, these tasks often require diverse and multi-step tool-use trajectories, which may lead to unnecessary video tool calls, incurring additional costs and failure risk. In this paper, we propose AdaVDR, an adaptive video deep research agent with adaptive tool use and reflection, which selects tools based on task and model capabilities while backtracking when needed. To this end, we develop a data construction pipeline that builds adaptive tool-use trajectories according to task types and model capabilities. Specifically, we construct QA pairs that require both video and external information, and organize the information acquisition processes into task-specific tool-use trajectories. We then apply model-conditioned tool necessity filtering to remove tools that can be bypassed using video understanding and internal knowledge of the model. Based on this pipeline, we construct a training dataset with adaptive trajectories and perform SFT on them to initialize these capabilities of AdaVDR. To further improve adaptive capabilities, we propose NASA-GRPO, a necessity-aware segment-guided credit assignment method, which evaluates segment-guided evidence contribution and tool necessity to construct normalized tool-level rewards. We also construct VDR-EE, a benchmark built using the proposed pipeline. Experiments show that AdaVDR outperforms the base model by 15.20 and 29.00 percentage points on VDR-EE and the existing VideoDR, respectively, demonstrating its superiority.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Discriminative Score Function: Turning Pretrained Models into Functional Generative Priors
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Discriminative models are trained with task-specific objectives such as classification, detection, or representation learning, yet their practical utility depends on generalizing beyond the training task to unseen samples from the same domain. This suggests that a discriminative model may retain an implicit trace of the data manifold beyond its task labels. We ask whether this trace can be exposed as a generative signal without task-specific guidance. We introduce the Discriminative Score Function (DSF), which extracts an image-space generative field from the loss-gradient geometry of a pretrained discriminative model. DSF provides a training-free update rule that moves images toward model-consistent visual regions without retraining or task-specific targets. We apply DSF to diverse pretrained discriminative models, including ResNet classifiers, DETR detectors, and DINOv2 ViT encoders. DSF generates unconditional images from noise and supports conditional guidance, editing, inpainting, and explanation through the same field. DSF-generated samples also provide effective zero-shot quantization calibration when real images or labels are unavailable, preserving feature geometry better than data-free calibration baselines. These results show that discriminative training leaves a generative functional signal for synthesis and calibration. Project page: https://junhoo.me/dsf.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 20 pages. Accepted at the Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (2026)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: HyperLoop: Hyperspectral-Assisted Loop Closure Detection in 3D-SLAM for Planetary Exploration
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Autonomous navigation of planetary rovers is challenged by visually repetitive, featureless terrain. SLAM systems based on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) offer dense mapping but rely on RGB appearance descriptors that degrade under perceptual aliasing - a common failure mode in extraterrestrial environments where physically distinct locations appear visually identical. This paper presents HyperLoop, the first framework integrating hyperspectral imaging (HSI) into the loop closure module of a 3DGS-based SLAM system. Hyperspectral descriptors encode material-level spectral signatures complementing RGB features, providing robustness to illumination changes and visual repetitiveness. Two HSI descriptor families are introduced: Bag-of-Spectral-Words (BoSW), encoding spectral material distributions via TF-IDF weighted histograms, and PCA-K VLAD (PCAK-VLAD), capturing first-order residual statistics of PCA-compressed spectral signatures. Both are evaluated with SIFT-VLAD and NetVLAD RGB descriptors under Strict-AND and Weighted fusion strategies on a custom dataset from the Moon-Mars Outdoor Test Site (MMOTS) at DLR, comprising synchronized RGB-D and hyperspectral sequences across four planetary analog traverses (65.5 m total). A key finding is that the sensor's Red-NIR range (600-860 nm) provides limited discriminability for rock terrain: the best HSI fusion (SIFT-VLAD + BoSW, Strict-AND) achieves 5.04 cm ATE RMSE, within 1.8% of SIFT-VLAD alone (4.95 cm). The gain over NetVLAD (8.81 cm) is attributable to SIFT-VLAD, not HSI fusion. This motivates future adoption of SWIR sensors capturing diagnostic mineral absorption features absent from the 600-860 nm range for planetary SLAM missions.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Paper accepted at International Astronautical Congress 2026, IAC-26,A3,IP,163,x107111

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Object Pose from 2-D to 3-D Point and Line Correspondences
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: In this paper we present a method for optimally estimating the rotation and translation between a camera and a 3-D object from point and/or line correspondences. First we devise an error function and second we show how to minimize this error function. The quadratic nature of this function is made possible by representing rotation and translation with a dual number quaternion. We provide a detailed account of the computational aspects of a trust-region optimization method. This method compares favourably with Newton's method which has extensively been used to solve the problem at hand, with Faugeras-Toscani linear method [6] for calibrating a camera, and with the Levenberg-Marquardt non-linear optimization method. Finally we present some experimental results which demonstrate the robustness of our method with respect to image noise and matching errors.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Measuring Epistemic Humility in Multimodal Large Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Hallucinations in multimodal large language models (MLLMs), where a model generates content inconsistent with the input image, pose significant risks in real-world applications. Existing hallucination benchmarks primarily test recognition, i.e., whether a model can select the correct answer among distractors. They overlook another capability that is essential for trustworthy AI: recognizing when none of the provided options is supported by the image and declining to commit to a false choice. We present HumbleBench, a hallucination benchmark that evaluates this false-option rejection behavior, a directly observable facet of epistemic humility, through multiple-choice questions that always include a "None of the above" (NOTA) option. HumbleBench is built from the Panoptic Scene Graph dataset: its object and relation annotations, together with candidate attribute cues, are used to prompt GPT-4-Turbo to generate questions, which are then manually verified, yielding 22,831 questions on object, relation, and attribute hallucinations. We evaluate 27 MLLMs, including general-purpose, reasoning-oriented, and proprietary models, and complement standard accuracy with NOTA-aware metrics, diagnostic stress tests, and a human evaluation. Even the strongest models select NOTA for only about half of the questions in which it is correct, cautious prompting shifts models toward NOTA without improving their ability to detect unsupported options, and humans reject unsupported options considerably more reliably than all evaluated models. These results show that recognition accuracy alone is insufficient for assessing hallucination robustness. Our code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/maifoundations/HumbleBench.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: A Diagnostic Study of World-Space Human Recovery Under High Camera Dynamics
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Monocular world-space human recovery methods excel on current benchmarks, but these rarely include fast camera motion. We introduce the K-Pop stress test, broadcast dance videos that combine fast, large camera motion with dense multi-person choreography. Leading methods produce plausible per-frame meshes on these videos, yet their world-space trajectories drift far from the performers' stage positions. Through a systematic diagnosis, we show that the camera and human estimates each remain self-consistent, and that the drift appears when they are combined at mismatched scales. Each is recovered at its own scale, so a mismatch between the two can turn camera motion into human drift that grows with camera displacement and becomes severe in broadcast dance videos. We derive a closed-form correction that estimates this mismatch and applies one scale to all performers, removing the drift while keeping their relative positions in one shared world frame. It requires no retraining and works with existing backends. Combined with physical constraints, the correction yields stable world-space reconstruction for choreography modeling, scene editing, data generation, and virtual reshooting.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Mitigating Video Hallucinations via Attention-Guided Representation Perturbation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Video large language models (Video LLMs) often generate responses unsupported by the input video. Contrastive decoding (CD) can mitigate these hallucinations, but its effectiveness depends on how the negative branch weakens visual evidence. Existing methods rely on predefined perturbations or masking guided by question reconstruction, offering limited control over the model's visual reliance during answer generation. We introduce Attention-guided Representation Perturbation for Contrastive Decoding (ARP-CD), a training-free framework for constructing contrastive negatives directly in representation space. ARP-CD uses the attention mass assigned to visual tokens at the answer-prediction position to guide bounded gradient updates of the language model's input visual hidden states. These updates reduce visual attention and produce a negative input, whose predictions are contrasted with those of the original branch throughout generation. Experiments across four Video LLMs and four benchmarks show that ARP-CD outperforms representative training-free baselines in most model--benchmark settings, reducing hallucinations while improving general video understanding. Further analyses show that attention-guided perturbation directions improve negative quality and that the resulting negatives provide effective contrastive references for correcting the original predictions.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Generative World Simulation with DAO and JING
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We present a Generative World Simulation framework that couples persistent shared world state with continuous first-person audiovisual generation. The framework integrates DAO, a computable world engine, and JING, an Egocentric Interactive Experience Model, to support sustained interaction for humans and agents. DAO maintains the states of characters, objects, and spaces and their relationships, advancing the world according to interaction rules and world time while preserving the consequences of past actions. From this evolving state, DAO derives observer-specific conditions for JING, which combines these conditions with character, object, and scene references, observation history, and current actions to generate each observer's audiovisual experience. Users can explore environments, manipulate objects, and communicate with characters through viewpoint control and text instructions, with their actions shaping both the shared state and subsequent experiences. By connecting world-state evolution with experience generation in a continuous interaction loop, the framework offers an approach to building interactive worlds that retain their history, evolve through action, and persist beyond any individual observer.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: XGEN DAO and JING Technical report. Contributors listed alphabetically by surname. Project page: https://xgenlabs.ai/research/generative-world-simulation; Model: https://huggingface.co/XGENlabs/XGEN-JING

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Recognizing Dialogue Ambiguity via Candidate Set Visual Grounding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Interpreting an ambiguous utterance in real-world interactions often requires context beyond a single utterance. When the utterance refers to objects in a visual scene, it is necessary to maintain and update the set of plausible referents as context accumulates, without assuming that the available information identifies a unique object. However, prior work on interactive visual grounding, which localizes objects referred to by linguistic expressions, has focused on identifying a unique object once sufficient dialogue context becomes available. To address this gap, we propose Candidate Set Visual Grounding (CSVG), a task for estimating the set of objects consistent with the given dialogue context. We further introduce CandVG, a benchmark that evaluates how the candidate set changes across dialogue turns. Our evaluation of vision-language models shows that stronger visual grounding capability does not necessarily yield better CSVG performance. In particular, models have difficulty predicting the complete candidate set, owing to challenges in candidate generation and premature commitment to a small set of candidates in early turns. Nevertheless, we find that this limitation can be partially mitigated in the evaluated large-scale models using instructions designed for CSVG.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: No Way To Steal My Face: Proactive Defense Against Identity-Preserving Personalized Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recent advances in diffusion models have enabled high-fidelity, identity-preserving image generation for personalized applications such as digital avatars and virtual try-on systems. However, their reliance on sensitive facial reference images raises growing privacy concerns. Existing defense mechanisms are primarily designed for training-based personalization and struggle to generalize to emerging training-free approaches, due to fundamental differences in their identity integration paradigms. To bridge this gap, we propose IDGuardian-the first generalizable and model-agnostic identity protection framework capable of defending against both training-based and training-free personalization methods. IDGuardian abstracts the personalization process into two critical stages: identity extraction and identity injection. It then introduces crafted adversarial perturbations to simultaneously disrupt both stages. Specifically, it degrades the identity features extracted by external encoders and establishes an adversarial conceptual bridge that misdirects the generative trajectory away from the target identity. Extensive experiments show that IDGuardian effectively protects identity across various personalization pipelines and model architectures, while remaining robust to post-processing, adaptive attacks, and cross-dataset generalization. Our code is available at https://github.com/OpenAscent-L/IDGuardian.git.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SceneAE: Scene Generation and Reconstruction in Queryable 3D-Anchored Latent Space
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
Recent video world models have increasingly adopted 3D memory mechanisms to integrate historical observations into a lightweight and persistent scene representation. This naturally raises a complementary question: if 3D representations can serve as an effective mechanism for memorizing observed scenes, can they also be directly used as the latent space for reconstructing and generating scenes? Motivated by this idea, we represent a scene as a compact and unstructured 3D-anchored latent space (\textbf{SceneAE}). Each latent combines an
  explicit 3D position with an implicit content feature and is spatially grounded to describe its local scene region, forming a
  sparse latent point cloud. Unlike conventional video-VAE latents that describe how a scene appears from particular viewpoints, our
  representation directly describes the scene itself, making it naturally applicable to both reconstruction and generation. For
  reconstruction, once the scene has been generated, our persistent 3D representation can be projected and decoded into RGB-D observations by different target cameras, without the need to regenerate a video for each new camera trajectory.
  For generation, we leverage the geometry-content separation to first generate camera-controlled 3D geometry and
  then synthesize content conditioned on it, reducing camera-appearance entanglement and improving camera
  controllability. Experiments show that this 3D latent achieves superior generation quality, computational cost, and camera controllability.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CLON: Cue-Calibrated Linguistic Object Onboarding for Zero-Shot 6D Pose Front-Ends
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Novel-object 6D pose pipelines depend on front-end hypotheses that retain target instances under clutter and occlusion without overwhelming downstream pose estimation. We introduce Cue-Calibrated Linguistic Object Onboarding (CLON), a training-free proposal-and-matching front-end. CLON converts multi-view CAD renderings into compact linguistic memories that provide object-specific conditioning to a frozen proposal generator. Constructed offline and reused across scenes, these memories augment generic prompts before segmentation; subsequent template verification assigns object identity. As a complementary onboarding step, CLON derives fixed cue weights from template statistics for semantic, appearance, and geometric verification. On seven BOP-Classic-Core datasets, CLON improves detection AP by 8.2 percentage points (pp), segmentation AP by 6.2 pp, and downstream pose AR by up to 4.1 pp over the evaluated CNOS and SAM-6D front-ends. In a real-world localization-to-grasp study under clutter and occlusion with 100 trials per method, CLON's improved localization doubles grasp success relative to the strongest evaluated baseline. Controlled ablations evaluate linguistic conditioning, multi-view construction, and verification. Analysis of a smaller candidate set with higher class-agnostic recall on five datasets.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PRIMEdit: Probability Redistribution for Instance-Aware Multi-Object Video Editing With a New Benchmark Dataset
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recent Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based video editing has enabled users to edit videos through simple text prompts, significantly simplifying the editing process. However, recent zero-shot video editing techniques focus on global or single-object edits, which can lead to unintended changes in other parts of the video. When editing multiple objects only within their localized regions, existing methods face challenges, such as unfaithful editing, editing leakage, and lack of suitable evaluation datasets and metrics. To overcome these limitations, we propose $\textbf{P}$robability $\textbf{R}$edistribution for $\textbf{I}$nstance-aware $\textbf{M}$ulti-object Video $\textbf{Edit}$ing ($\textbf{PRIMEdit}$). PRIMEdit is a zero-shot framework that introduces two key modules: (i) Instance-centric Probability Redistribution (IPR) to ensure precise localization and faithful editing and (ii) Disentangled Multi-instance Sampling (DMS) to prevent editing leakage. Additionally, we present the MIVE dataset for multi-instance video editing, including its subsets categorized by instance counts and sizes for controlled analysis across different levels of scene complexity. We also introduce the Cross-Instance Accuracy (CIA) Score that is firstly proposed to evaluate the editing leakage in multi-instance video editing tasks, which exhibits strong correlation with human evaluation as measured by Spearman's $ρ= 0.86$. Our extensive qualitative, quantitative, and user study evaluations demonstrate that PRIMEdit significantly outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods in terms of editing faithfulness, accuracy, and leakage prevention, setting a new benchmark for multi-instance video editing.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted manuscript published in IEEE TPAMI, vol. 48, no. 11, pp. 15571-15588, Nov. 2026. The first two authors contributed equally to this work. The last two authors are co-corresponding authors. Please visit our project page at https://kaist-viclab.github.io/primedit-site/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Enhancing Latent World Models with Associative Memory
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: World models trained via latent dynamics offer a scalable path for embodied planning, yet existing methods suffer from representational collapse, computational overhead, and limited long-horizon capability. We introduce a memory-enhanced latent world model that augments JEPA-style prediction with a content-addressable memory bank. Our approach learns high-level representations directly from observations, operating at multiple temporal scales within a shared latent space, and conditions predictions via adaptive layer normalization. To prevent collapse and ensure effective memory usage, we design two complementary losses that encourage slot diversity and balanced temporal utilization. Experiments on PushT, Tworoom, Reacher, and OGBCube demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance with a lightweight architecture, outperforming conventional latent world models on long-horizon planning tasks.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MicroSDF: Microfacet-Driven Hybrid Neural SDFs for Mixed-Reflectance Surface Reconstruction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Accurate 3D reconstruction in real-world environments remains a significant challenge due to the coexistence of reflective and non-reflective surfaces, which pose distinct modeling demands. Existing methods often treat these surface types separately, limiting their generalizability and physical plausibility. To bridge this gap, we propose MicroSDF, a novel neural implicit framework that facilitates geometry and reflectance modeling through microfacet theory. Our approach incorporates three core innovations: (i) a microfacet-guided geometry model that extracts multi-scale surface normals (macroscopic and microfacet) from a signed distance field (SDF), regularized by a proposed microfacet normal consistency loss to enforce physically plausible surface orientations; (ii) an enhanced dual-branch color model, where the specular branch leverages the microfacet normals to model high-frequency reflectance, and the vanilla branch, unlike prior works, uses reflection direction (instead of viewing direction) to better model diffuse and low-frequency specular components; and (iii) a detection-guided color blending strategy that adaptively fuses the color outputs based on reflection priors, providing more physically intuitive blending than implicitly learned blending weights. Combined with a tailored multi-stage optimization scheme, the proposed MicroSDF achieves robust and high-fidelity reconstruction across reflective and non-reflective surfaces. Extensive experiments on DTU, Shiny Blender, Ref-NeRF, and DeepVoxels datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, establishing a new direction for physically grounded neural reconstruction.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Published in IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, vol. 35, pp. 4106-4121, Apr. 2026. DOI: 10.1109/TIP.2026.3678096

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MIRAGE: Metric Inference and Reliability-Aware Gaussian Estimation from Feed-Forward Vision
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Feed-forward 3D priors enable high-quality reconstruction from image streams but often lack reliable metric scale and suffer from long-term trajectory drift. In contrast, LiDAR--inertial estimation provides metrically accurate motion but lacks the image-space consistency needed for high-fidelity reconstruction. We propose $MIRAGE$, which anchors feed-forward visual geometry to LiDAR--IMU metric motion and regulates online pose corrections according to correspondence support and cross-modal agreement, jointly enabling accurate metric pose estimation and high-fidelity Gaussian reconstruction. Experiments on Oxford Spires, M2DGR and INS show that MIRAGE achieves accurate metric trajectory estimation, outperforming COLMAP, a widely used but computationally expensive reference for vision-only benchmarks. Motivated by the scarcity of long-horizon monocular benchmarks for large-scale indoor reconstruction, we further build a multimodal data-collection platform and use MIRAGE to establish accurate 6-DoF reference trajectories for a new vision-only benchmark. We benchmark recent monocular large-scale reconstruction methods on this dataset, providing a systematic evaluation of their performance in long-horizon indoor scenes.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Remember, Revisit, Revise: Scaffold Memory for Long-Horizon 3D Geometry
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Geometry foundation models estimate camera poses and 3D scene structure from video sequences, but maintaining consistent reconstructions over long horizons remains challenging. Feed-forward models process long sequences as independent, fixed-length frame windows and align their predictions, causing pose and reconstruction errors to accumulate across windows. Streaming models retain information from past frames to inform future predictions, but cannot revise earlier estimates when later observations reveal errors. To address this, we introduce Scaffold MemOry for Revision (SMORE), a framework equipping frozen geometry foundation models with a revisable external memory for long-horizon inference. Inspired by hippocampal associative memory in biological brains, which links spatial context with sensory experience, SMORE associates where an observer is with what it observes, enabling past observations to be stored, retrieved, verified against new evidence, and revised when inconsistencies are detected. We evaluate SMORE with eight competitive geometry models on five datasets spanning camera pose estimation, multi-view depth estimation, 3D point-cloud reconstruction, simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), and novel view synthesis. Across all evaluated models, SMORE consistently improves long-sequence pose estimation, reduces multi-view depth error by up to 58%, reduces Chamfer distance for 3D point-cloud reconstruction by up to 43%, and achieves average trajectory error as low as 2.9 cm in long-horizon SLAM. By retaining corrected poses and observations, SMORE further improves the fidelity and spatial consistency of large-scale 3D scene reconstruction. These results establish revisable external memory as a flexible interface for extending pretrained geometry models beyond fixed-context prediction toward iterative, error-correcting inference over long visual sequences.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Video Depth Anything: Consistent Depth Estimation for Super-Long Videos
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Depth Anything has achieved remarkable success in monocular depth estimation with strong generalization ability. However, it suffers from temporal inconsistency in videos, hindering its practical applications. Various methods have been proposed to alleviate this issue by leveraging video generation models or introducing priors from optical flow and camera poses. Nonetheless, these methods are only applicable to short videos (< 10 seconds) and require a trade-off between quality and computational efficiency. We propose Video Depth Anything for high-quality, consistent depth estimation in super-long videos (over several minutes) without sacrificing efficiency. We base our model on Depth Anything V2 and replace its head with an efficient spatial-temporal head. We design a straightforward yet effective temporal consistency loss by constraining the temporal depth gradient, eliminating the need for additional geometric priors. The model is trained on a joint dataset of video depth and unlabeled images, similar to Depth Anything V2. Moreover, a novel key-frame-based strategy is developed for long video inference. Experiments show that our model can be applied to arbitrarily long videos without compromising quality, consistency, or generalization ability. Comprehensive evaluations on multiple video benchmarks demonstrate that our approach sets a new state-of-the-art in zero-shot video depth estimation. We offer models of different scales to support a range of scenarios, with our smallest model capable of real-time performance at 30 FPS.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Plan-Bench: Can Existing VLMs Go Well Beyond Perception to Reason and Plan in Embodied Worlds?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in visual perception and spatial reasoning, leading to growing interest in using them as high-level planners for embodied AI. However, physical tasks require models to integrate spatial information, reason over temporal states, and generate multi-step plans under various constraints, raising the question of whether current VLMs can reliably support such reasoning and planning independently of execution. We introduce Plan-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating the high-level reasoning and multi-step planning capabilities of VLMs relevant to embodied worlds, while isolating the influence of action execution. It covers three complementary dimensions, spanning 16 subclasses and 699 curated samples. Extensive evaluation of 28 VLMs reveals room for improvement, with even the strongest model achieving only 75.0% accuracy. We further find that model scaling generally improves these capabilities. Ablation studies also indicate larger models show increasing potential as high-level planners. Overall, Plan-Bench provides a lightweight probe for evaluating VLMs' reasoning and planning capabilities relevant to embodied environments and assessing their potential as decision makers for physical tasks. Our benchmark and code are available at https://github.com/MinneFeng/Plan-Bench.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Off-the-Shelf Language-Vision Encoders Predict Human Gaze Preferences in Visual World Experiments
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: A central question for computational psycholinguistics is to what extent neural language models can serve as cognitively adequate models of human language processing. However, work has been overwhelmingly focused on the unimodal case of written or spoken language. In contrast, multimodal paradigms, like visual world experiments that present participants with both visual and linguistic input simultaneously, have been neglected. In this paper, we present a novel approach that predicts patterns of gaze preferences in visual world studies. To do so, it derives target preferences by applying an attribution method to a simple bi-modal CLIP bi-encoder. We demonstrate the ability of this approach to qualitatively replicate the gaze patterns found in a seminal English visual world study demonstrating human predictive processing. It does so without a generative architecture and without the need for fine-tuning, despite not being trained for the task.
